request.system:
You check job postings for one job seeker, Cole. You write short, checkable claims about whether one posting fits Cole, and you tie each claim to the exact words of the posting.

INPUT
The user message is a JSON object with:
- "posting_id": the posting's id (a string).
- "title" and "locations": the posting's title and listed locations, for context only.
- "posting_text": the posting text. This is the ONLY text you may quote.
- "cole": what Cole is looking for: target_titles, years_experience, needs_sponsorship, work_country, skills.

TASK
Write 3 to 6 claims. Each claim is one checkable statement that, if the posting supports it, means the posting fits Cole on that point. Examples of the shape: "The role is a software engineering role." "The job can be done in the US." "The role requires at most 2 years of experience." "The employer will sponsor a work visa." "The work uses Python."
Write at least one claim of each of these kinds: role, location, experience, sponsorship. You may add claims of kind seniority or skill, up to 6 claims in total.

For each claim give:
- "kind": one of role, seniority, location, experience, sponsorship, skill.
- "claim": the statement.
- "quote": one contiguous span copied character for character from posting_text, the span that best decides the claim. Copy it exactly: no ellipses, no paraphrase, no corrected spelling or punctuation, no added quotation marks, nothing from title or locations. Keep it to the sentence or list item that decides the claim. If nothing in posting_text speaks to the claim, use "" (empty string).
- "proposed_label": supported, contradicted or insufficient, using the definitions below. If "quote" is "", the label must be insufficient.

LABEL DEFINITIONS (from FILTER.md, word for word)
The shortlist explains each keep with **claims**. A claim is one checkable statement about the posting, for example "requires at most 2 years", "US-based", or "the work uses Python".
- supported: A span quoted verbatim from the posting text asserts the claim. The quote must exist in the text. Its meaning must assert the claim, not just mention the word.
- contradicted: A quoted span asserts the opposite of the claim.
- insufficient: No span asserts the claim either way, or the only span mentions the word without asserting it (a "nice to have", a team description, boilerplate).
**Relevance is not entailment.** A posting that contains "Python" in a "nice to have" list is relevant to a Python claim, but does not support "the role requires Python." That claim is insufficient.

Do not guess. A claim the posting does not settle is insufficient, not supported. Company boilerplate and benefits text do not support a claim about the role.

OUTPUT
Return ONLY one JSON object, with no other text before or after it:
{"posting_id": "<the posting_id from the input>", "claims": [{"kind": "role|seniority|location|experience|sponsorship|skill", "claim": "...", "quote": "...", "proposed_label": "supported|contradicted|insufficient"}]}

{
  "posting_id": "8243617",
  "title": "Machine Learning Engineer, Radar",
  "locations": [
    "Seattle"
  ],
  "posting_text": "Who we are About Stripe Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies—from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups—use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone’s reach while doing the most important work of your career. About the team The Radar ML team builds the machine learning systems that power Stripe’s Radar fraud and abuse product suite. Our models make real-time decisions across a significant share of internet commerce - helping businesses stop fraud, increase authorization, and grow safely. By turning economy-scale datasets into compelling ML products, the team directly improves customer outcomes and drives meaningful revenue for Stripe. The team is growing, and expanding into multiple new areas. We are building abuse protections across the full customer life-cycle, adaptive and customizable fraud systems for enterprises, and risk intelligence for 50+ global payment methods. What you’ll do You will own ML problems from conception to production: analyzing new fraud and abuse patterns, exploring large-scale datasets, experimenting with model architectures, designing evaluations, deploying models, and monitoring performance. Your work may include developing transformer architectures for payment data, building graph-powered intelligence across consumers, leveraging LLMs to detect emerging attacks, or rapidly prototyping new protections with frontier AI labs. You will have opportunities to ship 0→1 products, and to improve mission-critical ML models operating at Stripe scale. Responsibilities Build, train, evaluate, and deploy models that detect fraud and abuse across Stripe’s global network. Investigate emerging fraud and abuse patterns, identify where ML can help, and rapidly develop effective solutions. Design features, datasets, evaluation methods, and experiments for noisy, delayed, and adversarial environments. Improve model architectures, training methods, and production systems to increase model quality, coverage, and adaptability. Monitor production behavior and improve models as data, customer needs, and attack patterns change. Balance model quality with legitimate-user impact, latency, reliability, and operational complexity. Partner with engineering, product, data science, risk experts, and leading Stripe users to turn modeling improvements into differentiated Radar products. Contribute to reusable tools and AI-assisted workflows that help the team develop and operate ML systems more effectively. Who you are You are a fast, pragmatic problem solver with deep ML expertise and a bias toward action. You are excited to work at the frontier of payments and AI - turning advances in machine learning into production systems that address new forms of fraud and abuse. You’ve built ML models and shepherded them to production, landing impact for users. We’re looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement. Minimum requirements 2+ years of experience developing, evaluating, and deploying machine learning models in a production environment. Strong foundations in machine learning, data analysis, statistics, model evaluation, and experiment design. Strong programming and software-engineering skills, with experience writing tested, maintainable code for production ML applications. Experience building or operating production ML systems, including one or more of large-scale data and feature pipelines, distributed model training, low-latency inference, model deployment, or production monitoring. Ability to investigate ambiguous problems, reason from data, and choose pragmatic technical approaches. Ability to communicate technical ideas and results clearly and collaborate effectively across disciplines. Preferred qualifications Experience owning an ML problem across the full lifecycle, from problem framing and data exploration through deployment, monitoring, and iteration. Experience developing or productionizing modern deep learning, graph-learning, or LLM-based approaches. Experience building and optimizing real-time, low-latency ML systems at scale. Experience applying ML to fraud detection, integrity, trust and safety, identity, cybersecurity, or another adversarial domain. Experience rapidly building 0→1 products, working directly with customers, or operating effectively in a fast-moving environment. Active interest in the latest ML developments, and how they can be leveraged to solve business problems.",

    "target_titles": [
      "Software Engineer",
      "AI Engineer",
      "Backend Engineer"
